commands.author: xydigit-zt

target.title: fix(security): add estimate-before-decode guard to base64 paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large base64-encoded images can cause transient memory pressure during decoding. This PR adds a size estimation check before decoding base64 image data in CLI staging and provider image-parsing paths, and propagates the existing configured media size limit through these new guards.

**Security impact**: Defense-in-depth against transient memory exhaustion from oversized base64 payloads.

## Summary

- Added `estimateBase64DecodedSize` helper that estimates decoded byte length from base64 input
- Propagated existing `maxBytes` limit through:
  - CLI image writing (`writeCliImages`)
  - Provider image parsing (`generatedImageAssetFromBase64`)
- Added boundary tests for:
  - Configured limit acceptance (7MB payload under 8MB limit)
  - Over-limit rejection before decoding
  - Default limit enforcement (6 MiB)
- **No new configuration**: Uses existing `generatedMediaMaxBytes` setting

## Evidence

**Environment**: macOS Vitest (Node 22.22.2)

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# Run configured limit test
npx vitest run src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts
```

**Observed result after fix**:
```text
✓ agents-core src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts (30 tests) 203ms
✓ agents-support src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts (30 tests) 184ms

Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  60 passed (60)

Key test coverage:
✓ rejects base64 image that exceeds size limit
✓ accepts images above MAX_IMAGE_BYTES when a higher configured maxBytes is provided
  - 7MB payload accepted under 8MB configured limit (line 322-346)
  - 10MB payload rejected under 8MB limit
  - 7MB payload rejected under default 6MiB limit (no maxBytes)
```

**Configuration limit propagation verified**:
- Test file: `src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts:322-346`
- Scenario: 7MB payload (above default 6MiB) accepted when 8MB limit configured
- Code path: `writeCliImages` receives `maxBytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024`, checks pass

**What was not tested**: Live provider OOM reproduction (neither necessary nor safely desirable)

## Regression Test Plan
- Coverage: 60 tests across 2 test suites
- Target files: `src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts`, `src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Estimated size < maxBytes: accept
  - Estimated size > maxBytes: reject before decode
  - Configured limit > default: use configured
  - No configured limit: use default 6 MiB

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Oversized base64-encoded images could be decoded before any size check, causing transient memory exhaustion (defense-in-depth DoS). The fix estimates decoded size via `estimateBase64DecodedSize` and rejects over-limit input **before** decoding in `writeCliImages` (CLI staging) and `generatedImageAssetFromBase64` (provider image parsing), propagating the existing `maxBytes`/`generatedMediaMaxBytes` limit.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9. The guard is exercised by the in-repo boundary tests that feed controlled base64 payloads (7MB / 8MB / 10MB) and assert accept/reject decisions before decode.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts`

Evidence after fix:
```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  60 passed (60)
 - rejects base64 image that exceeds size limit
 - accepts 7MB payload under 8MB configured limit (line 322-346)
 - rejects 10MB payload under 8MB limit
 - rejects 7MB payload under default 6MiB limit (no maxBytes)
```

Observed result after fix: Payloads exceeding the configured/default media size limit are rejected before any `Buffer.from(data, "base64")` decode, so oversized input cannot trigger transient memory pressure. Configured limits above the default are honored. No new configuration surface was added (uses existing `generatedMediaMaxBytes`).

What was not tested: Live provider out-of-memory reproduction was not run (neither necessary nor safely desirable); the proof targets the exact changed guard branches with synthetic over-limit payloads.
